answer: Interleaved Arrival Timing. Each identity must forge a request history whose gaps match a seeded traffic curve; the gate rejects bursts that arrive faster than the curve allows. A quill of randomized delays is issued per identity and checked against later traffic, so mass-registered accounts drift out of shape. Attackers must then pay real elapsed time and scheduling overhead per identity, and one mis-timed shale of traffic collapses the whole batch.
